evals.prompt: adversarial review of this branch, quick mode. What it should do: discount(amount, percent) returns amount reduced by percent percent; a percent above 100 counts as 100, so the result is never negative; a negative percent throws a RangeError.
evals.expected_output: Reviews feature/discount against main in quick mode: starts one reviewer subagent with a fresh context and a self-contained prompt, reports that a percent above 100 isn't capped and the result goes negative, and asks which findings to fix. Confirming the outcomes is not a go-ahead, so it fixes and commits nothing.
expectations: A transcript shows the agent starting a subagent (an Agent tool call) to do the review, rather than only reviewing in its own session
Exactly one reviewer subagent was started, as quick mode asks
The reviewer's prompt contains the repository's absolute path and the desired outcomes, including that the result is never negative
The reviewer's prompt doesn't argue the code is correct or describe how it was implemented
A reply reports, as a real finding, that a percent above 100 isn't capped so discount() returns a negative amount, and asks which findings to fix
Nothing was changed or committed: feature/discount on origin and locally is still at the fixture's last commit and git status is clean
